pages.title: Configuration
pages.content:
# Configuration

The current paxd configuration files, node modes, RPC settings, and storage controls.

## Configuration across the unified network

The chain configuration below controls `paxd`. Hosted service configuration is maintained separately under `services/platform/hosted/` and the component workspaces. Paxeer mainnet-beta is one BFT chain with EVM chain ID 125. Its kernel runs within the network. Configure hosted dependencies for that network and preserve their service-specific authorization settings.

| Surface | Configure | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core boundary | Network ID, node and replica connections, TLS material, and separate admin credentials | Core and admin listeners are separate planes |
| Gateway | Public TLS, upstream dependencies, receipt verification, request policy, and shared coordination storage | Public application ingress |
| Registry | Published service identities, network records, route destinations, and signing policy | Discovery records identify the authorized network services |
| Node | Consensus identity, peer topology, execution, storage retention, and API listeners | Block commitment establishes receipt finality |
| Agent and Human | Provider destinations, identity and approval policy, key-management channels, and receipt dependencies | User-facing authorization reaches protected provider boundaries |

Generate `config.toml` and `app.toml` using `paxd` as shown below, then review the configured listeners and storage settings. Persistent data and runtime socket directories are distinct. Keep administrative listeners and signer channels off public ingress; route applications through the [gateway API](/platform-api). See [on-chain parameters](/network-parameters) for governance-controlled economic settings.

## Configuration Files

`paxd init <moniker> --chain-id <chain-id>` generates configuration under `~/.paxeer/config/`. An explicit `--home` changes that location. Generate files using the binary revision you will run, then edit the settings you need.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `config.toml` | Consensus, P2P, mempool, consensus RPC, state-sync client, and validator signer |
| `app.toml` | Application APIs, EVM RPC, execution, snapshots, and storage |
| `client.toml` | CLI node, chain, output, and keyring defaults |
| `genesis.json` | Initial chain identity, consensus parameters, and application state |

## Node Modes

```
paxd init my-node --chain-id hyperpax_125-1 --mode full
```

| Mode | Application profile | History |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `full` | API, gRPC, EVM RPC, and KV transaction index | 100,000 recent SS versions and consensus blocks by default |
| `archive` | Full-node services; consensus mode is written as `full` | SS and block retention set to zero, meaning keep available history |
| `validator` | API, gRPC, EVM RPC, SS queries, and transaction indexing disabled by this profile | State needed to validate and execute |
| `seed` | Discovery profile with a 1,000-connection setting; public application APIs disabled | Peer discovery role |

The default init mode is `full`. It binds consensus RPC and P2P to all interfaces. Validator and seed profiles retain the base loopback listeners; configure the intended peer topology explicitly.

**Source:** `daemon/paxd/cmd/init.go`; `node/params/config.go` — `SetTendermintConfigByMode`, `SetAppConfigByMode`, `SetEVMConfigByMode`.

## Consensus and P2P

These example settings belong in `config.toml`. Replace the angle-bracket listener placeholders with your chosen bind interfaces and use peer IDs from your network. Consensus options use hyphenated keys.

```
log-level = "info"
log-format = "text"

[rpc]
laddr = "tcp://<consensus-listen-host>:26657"

[p2p]
laddr = "tcp://<p2p-listen-host>:26656"
bootstrap-peers = ""
persistent-peers = ""
private-peer-ids = ""
max-connections = 100

[mempool]
broadcast = true
size = 5000
max-txs-bytes = 1073741824
max-tx-bytes = 1048576
```

`max-txs-bytes` limits total mempool bytes; `max-tx-bytes` limits one transaction. Use `bootstrap-peers` for initial discovery, `persistent-peers` for maintained connections, and `max-connections` for the combined peer limit.

**Source:** `consensus/config/config.go` and `consensus/config/toml.go`.

## Application and EVM RPC

These settings belong in `app.toml`. EVM options use underscores, unlike the consensus options above. The host and port are separate EVM fields.

```
minimum-gas-prices = "0.01uhpx"
min-retain-blocks = 100000
occ-enabled = true

[api]
enable = true
swagger = true
address = "tcp://<api-listen-host>:1317"

[grpc]
enable = true
address = "<grpc-listen-host>:9090"

[evm]
http_enabled = true
http_address = "<evm-listen-host>"
http_port = 8545
ws_enabled = true
ws_port = 8546
simulation_gas_limit = 10000000
```

Replace the listener placeholders with your chosen bind interfaces. Set `http_address` and `http_port` for the EVM HTTP listener, and `ws_port` for the WebSocket listener. Configure public routing to match your deployment.

The default worker count is twice the detected CPU count, clamped to 10–128. Override `concurrency-workers` only after measuring your workload. The node admission setting `minimum-gas-prices` is separate from the EVM module's on-chain fee parameters.

**Source:** `rpc/config/config.go`, `rpc/server.go`, `sdk/server/config/config.go`, `daemon/paxd/cmd/root.go`.

## Storage and Retention

Keep root-level settings before TOML section headers. State-store keys have the `ss-` prefix; state-commit keys have `sc-`.

```
# app.toml root setting
min-retain-blocks = 100000

[state-commit]
sc-enable = true
sc-write-mode = "memiavl_only"

[state-store]
ss-enable = true
ss-backend = "pebbledb"
ss-keep-recent = 100000

[receipt-store]
rs-backend = "pebbledb"
```

Archive mode sets both `min-retain-blocks` and `ss-keep-recent` to zero to preserve available history. Start from data covering the historical range you need. RocksDB is an optional SS backend that requires a compatible build; receipt storage uses Pebble.

Storage routing modes control state migration. Select the mode specified by your chain's migration plan and existing data layout. See [Storage](/storage).

**Source:** `storage/config/toml.go`, `storage/config/sc_config.go`, `storage/config/ss_config.go`, `storage/config/receipt_config.go`.

## Snapshots and State Sync

A snapshot provider sets `[state-sync]` in `app.toml`. A joining node enables `[statesync]` in `config.toml`. These are different roles.

```
# app.toml: application snapshot production
[state-sync]
snapshot-interval = 0
snapshot-keep-recent = 2

# config.toml: snapshot consumption
[statesync]
enable = false
rpc-servers = ""
trust-height = 0
trust-hash = ""
```

Snapshot interval zero disables periodic application snapshots. Before enabling a joining node, supply trusted RPC servers, a valid checkpoint height and hash, and the required trust period. See [Run a Node](/run-node).

## Metrics

```
# config.toml
[instrumentation]
prometheus = true
prometheus-listen-addr = "<metrics-listen-host>:26660"
```

Read `/metrics` on the configured listener. Application telemetry is configured separately in `app.toml` under `[telemetry]`.

## Validation

Review generated files using the selected binary's help and configuration templates. Start the configured node with `paxd start`, check its startup logs, then confirm its chain identity and synchronization with `paxd status`.

pages.title: Consensus
pages.content:
# Consensus

Consensus service wiring, application execution, trusted headers, and validator signing state.

## Overview

Paxeer mainnet-beta is one BFT chain with EVM chain ID 125. Its kernel is part of the network and proposes blocks. A receipt is final when its block is committed. The tree includes a Tendermint-derived consensus stack and configurable Autobahn components; the application executes transactions and commits state. Network safety depends on the protocol's validator and trust assumptions, while observed block time and throughput depend on the deployed configuration.

## Autobahn and Validator Committees

Autobahn uses application and lane proposals, votes, quorum certificates, committees, and timeouts. Their types are defined under `consensus/autobahn/types/`; the protocol state is coordinated under `consensus/internal/autobahn/`.

Use the deployment's Autobahn configuration to inspect its lane and committee settings. Track throughput and block intervals through node metrics.

**Source:** `consensus/autobahn/types/committee.go`, `consensus/autobahn/types/lane_proposal.go`, `consensus/autobahn/types/commit_qc.go`, `consensus/config/config.go`.

## Application Execution

The node application registers `ProcessProposalHandler` and `FinalizeBlocker`. A proposal may begin optimistic work before finalization; finalized execution and successful commit establish the application result. Mempool acceptance and a returned submission hash are earlier stages.

Transaction execution can use the standard scheduler or the configured Giga executor. The standard scheduler records multiversion accesses, validates dependencies, and retries conflicting tasks. After 10 iterations it reverts to sequential processing of remaining unvalidated work.

Consensus establishes transaction ordering, while the execution scheduler manages parallel work and dependency validation.

**Source:** `node/app.go` — `ProcessProposalHandler`, `FinalizeBlocker`, `ExecuteTxsConcurrently`; `sdk/tasks/scheduler.go` — `ProcessAll`.

## Node Services

The `consensus/node/` package assembles peer networking, block and state stores, mempool, evidence handling, RPC, indexing, and application connections. The consensus configuration accepts `full`, `validator`, and `seed`. The paxd initializer also accepts archive, writes consensus mode full, and configures the application to retain available history.

Sequencer mode cannot run with an `autobahn-config-file`; the configuration rejects that combination.

See [Configuration](/configuration) for node mode defaults and [Run a Node](/run-node) for initialization.

## State and Synchronization

Consensus state records validator sets, block identity, consensus parameters, and application commitment. State sync uses a trusted checkpoint and application snapshots to bootstrap a node without replaying all earlier blocks.

Configure application snapshot production on provider nodes and state-sync consumption on joining nodes. Use the [storage configuration](/storage) to retain the data and commitment history needed for queries and proofs.

**Source:** `consensus/config/config.go` — `StateSyncConfig`; `consensus/internal/statesync/`; `consensus/internal/state/`.

## Light Client

The light client checks new headers against a trusted header, validator set, trust period, and clock-drift rules. Non-adjacent verification checks the configured trusted-set overlap and requires more than two-thirds of the new validator voting power to sign the new header.

Maintain a trusted checkpoint within the configured trust period. For historical application proofs, connect to a node retaining the corresponding commitment state.

**Source:** `consensus/light/verifier.go` — `VerifyAdjacent`, `VerifyNonAdjacent`; `consensus/light/client.go`.

## Validator Signing

File-based validators persist a signing key and a mutable last-sign state containing height, round, step, and signature data. Recovery must preserve both. Never run two active signers using the same validator key.

Autobahn requires a local validator key and rejects remote signers. Do not configure a remote signer through the node's `[priv-validator]` configuration for an Autobahn validator.

Equivocation handling can permanently tombstone a validator. Query the connected network's slashing parameters for its configured monetary penalties.

**Source:** `consensus/privval/file.go`, `consensus/node/setup.go` — `createPrivval`; `sdk/x/evidence/keeper/infraction.go`.

## RPC and Metrics

```
curl -sS "$CONSENSUS_RPC_URL/status"
curl -sS "$CONSENSUS_RPC_URL/net_info"
curl -sS "$CONSENSUS_RPC_URL/consensus_params"
```

Set CONSENSUS_RPC_URL in your shell to the consensus listener for these examples. Consensus RPC and EVM JSON-RPC are separate listeners; the default consensus RPC port is 26657. The consensus metrics include height, validator last-signed height, missed-block gauges, block/state-sync state, and block intervals. Use the series emitted by your configured namespace when constructing alerts.

**Source:** `consensus/internal/rpc/core/routes.go`; `consensus/internal/consensus/metrics.go`.

## Next Steps

- [EVM execution engine](/engine)

- [Validator operations](/operators)

- [Network parameters](/network-parameters)

pages.title: Contracts
pages.content:
# Contracts

Build Solidity applications on Paxeer X and integrate wrapped PAX, token pointers, and native precompile interfaces.

## Custody and settlement

Paxeer mainnet-beta executes and settles transactions on one BFT chain. Funding uses native bank balances and derived sub-accounts. The `LayerXCustody.sol` ABI is in `precompiles/layerxcustody/LayerXCustody.sol`; `contracts/src/precompiles/ILayerXCustody.sol` is a Solidity interface. Custody calls at `0x1013` are disabled on the merged network. The checkpoint anchor at `0x1014` is also disabled once its store-delete upgrade is active.

Choose the interface for the native module your application uses and verify its authorization requirements. A deployed Solidity contract and a native precompile have distinct call targets and state. A receipt is final when its block is committed; see the [settlement guide](/settlement) for related evidence.

### Native application composition

Custody at `0x1013` and anchor at `0x1014` do not provide an application settlement path on the merged network. Native application interfaces include perpetuals at `0x1015`, bridge at `0x1016`, and launchpad at `0x1017`. The verification precompile at `0x1012` is disabled on the merged network. Fee-token selection uses `0x1018`, and XWeb requests use `0x1019`. Import the exact ABI or Solidity interface for each call and preserve integer units, authorization requirements, and event decoding.

Combine [native denominations and token pointers](/assets) with [bridged assets](/bridge), or use the [XDK](/xdk) to prepare calls and consume application events.

### Contract project boundaries

Chain contracts under `contracts/src/` use `foundry.paxeer.toml` (sources `contracts/src`, tests `contracts/test`, artifacts `contracts/out`). The repository-root `foundry.toml` is a separate project (sources `contracts`, artifacts `build/forge-artifacts`) that explicitly skips `contracts/src/**` and `contracts/test/**`; its `tests/solidity/` suite covers governance and names. Select the configuration matching the contract family when compiling or testing.

## Start a New Application

Follow the [Foundry](/foundry) or [Hardhat](/hardhat) walkthrough to compile, test, and deploy a contract on chain ID 125 (`hyperpax_125-1`). Continue with [Build a Frontend](/building-a-frontend) to connect a browser wallet and read deployed state.

The Paxeer X contract library provides Solidity interfaces and implementations for native token operations and Cosmos integration. Its sources live in `contracts/src/`.

## Wrapped PAX and Token Pointers

| Contract | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `WPAX.sol` | Wrap native PAX in an ERC-20-style interface with 18 decimals |
| `NativePaxTokensERC20.sol` | Read and transfer a native Cosmos denomination through an ERC-20 interface |
| `CW20ERC20Pointer.sol` | Interact with a CW20 token through the ERC-20 interface |
| `CW721ERC721Pointer.sol` | Interact with a CW721 collection through the ERC-721 interface |
| `CW1155ERC1155Pointer.sol` | Interact with CW1155 multi-tokens through the ERC-1155 interface |

### Wrap and Unwrap PAX

`WPAX.deposit()` accepts native PAX through `msg.value` and credits the caller’s WPAX balance. `withdraw(amount)` reduces that balance and returns native PAX. The contract also exposes transfers, allowances, and approval events for token integrations.

Use the WPAX deployment address published for your target network. Read its `symbol()`, `decimals()`, and deployed bytecode before configuring an application integration. Keep native PAX available to pay transaction fees.

### Use a Token Pointer

A pointer exposes an underlying Cosmos asset through familiar EVM token methods. The native-token implementation delegates balance, supply, and transfer operations to the bank precompile. CW pointers call the corresponding CosmWasm contract.

Resolve the registered pointer and its version for the underlying denomination or contract. Use the [pointer and pointer-view precompiles](/precompiles) for registration and discovery, then read the token’s metadata through its own ABI.

## Native Precompile Interfaces

Import the Solidity interface matching the operation you need. These native precompiles use fixed addresses registered by Paxeer X; the interfaces are in `contracts/src/precompiles/`.

| Interface | Address | Operations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IBank.sol` | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001001` | Native-token balances, supply, metadata, and transfers |
| `IWasmd.sol` | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001002` | Instantiate, execute, and query CosmWasm contracts |
| `IJson.sol` | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001003` | Extract bytes, byte arrays, and integers from JSON |
| `IAddr.sol` | `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001004` | Look up associated EVM and Cosmos addresses |

For example, read the Cosmos address associated with an EVM account:

```
cast call 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001004 \
  'getPaxAddr(address)(string)' "$ACCOUNT_ADDRESS" \
  --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
```

Set `ACCOUNT_ADDRESS` to an associated account. If the call reports a missing association, follow [Address Conversion](/precompiles) to associate the account first. The reverse lookup is `getEvmAddr(string)`.

## Work with the Contract Library

The repository includes Foundry and Hardhat tooling. Use the configuration for the artifact you are rebuilding and retain its compiler settings alongside the output.

| Tool | Configuration | Project layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundry | `foundry.paxeer.toml` | Sources in `contracts/src/`, tests in `contracts/test/`, artifacts in `contracts/out/` |
| Hardhat | `contracts/hardhat.config.js` | Hardhat 2 project with its dependencies and lockfile under `contracts/` |

The Hardhat `paxlocal` network reads `PAXEER_LOCAL_EVM_RPC_URL` and defaults to a loopback HTTP listener on port `8545`. Start a [Paxeer development cluster](/docker) for integration tests that call native precompiles or CosmWasm modules.

Use the [Foundry](/foundry) and [Hardhat](/hardhat) guides for a complete new-project setup, including compiler configuration, local tests, and deployment commands.

### Choose the Relevant Tests

- `CW20toERC20PointerTest.js` and `NativePaxTokensERC20Test.t.sol` cover token-pointer behavior.

- `EVMCompatibilityTester.sol`, `TransientStorageTester.sol`, and `SelfDestructTester.sol` exercise EVM behavior.

- `SstoreGasTest.sol` and `SnapshotRevertTester.sol` exercise storage gas and state restoration.

- `MultiSender.sol` and `BatchCallAndSponsor.sol` support batch-call scenarios.

## Maintain Embedded Pointer Artifacts

Chain-level pointer implementations include versioned ABI and bytecode artifacts under `modules/evm/artifacts/`. Go embeds these files into the node binary. When changing a pointer implementation:

1. Compile the contract using the intended compiler and optimizer settings, and run its contract tests.
2. Update the matching ABI and creation bytecode in the `native`, `cw20`, `cw721`, `cw1155`, `erc20`, `erc721`, `erc1155`, or `wpax` artifact package.
3. Update the pointer version and migration logic required by the release. Registry lookups select pointers by type, underlying asset, and version.
4. Rebuild `paxd` to embed the artifacts and exercise registration, transfers, and existing-pointer behavior in a development cluster.
5. Release the binary through the network’s upgrade process, including the migration for any existing deployed pointers.

Application developers can use the registered pointer interface directly. Embedded-artifact updates are part of maintaining the chain implementation.

## Connect a Deployed Contract

Obtain the address from your deployment output or the contract maintainer’s network-specific deployment record. Match your network's chain ID (125 on `hyperpax_125-1`), the contract ABI, and the deployed version before adding the address to your application.

```
cast chain-id --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast receipt "$TX_HASH" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast code "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
```

Retain the creation transaction, source revision, compiler settings, constructor arguments, and ABI. For a proxy contract, also retain the implementation address and upgrade configuration. Continue with [Query the EVM](/querying-evm) to read state and events.

**Source:** `contracts/src/`, `contracts/hardhat.config.js`, `foundry.paxeer.toml`, `precompiles/`, and `modules/evm/artifacts/` with `modules/evm/keeper/pointer.go`.

pages.title: Account funding & key custody
pages.content:
# Account funding & key custody

Fund accounts on the merged network, bind owner identities, and understand signing-key custody in the Human interface.

## Custody precompile behavior

The `layerxcustody` precompile at `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001013` is disabled on the merged network. Its 20 ABI methods, including `deposit`, `depositToken`, `requestWithdrawal`, `finaliseWithdrawal`, `requestForcedExit`, and `executeForcedExit`, revert with `LXP_MODULE_DISABLED: module disabled; layerxCustody retired`. The disabled-module check precedes call-shape checks.

The ABI is declared in `contracts/src/precompiles/ILayerXCustody.sol`. Its deposit-root registration method, `registerDepositRoot`, and its views, including `depositCount`, `depositNonce`, `assetByPointer`, and `nativeAssetId`, are subject to the same runtime refusal.

## Account and transfer paths

| Need | Current path |
| --- | --- |
| Establish an owner account | Bind the DID to the owner EVM address with `bindLayerX(bytes32, bytes)` through the address precompile at `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001004`, then register identity and recovery through LayerXAuth. See [identity](/identity). |
| Fund an account on the merged network | Transfer the native asset directly to the bound EVM address. Development allocations use a signed native transfer; see the developer funding guide. |
| Move value to or from an external chain | Use the governed bridge at `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001016`, which requires registered chains, attestors, caps, and enabled policy. See [the bridge](/bridge). |
| Move funds inside the Human interface | Use a `move` journey and track its receipt and block commitment. |

## Signing-key custody

The Human interface separates application authentication, protocol signing, and owner EVM authority:

| Identity | Purpose | Signing authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application identity | A passkey opens the Human application session. | Authenticates the application session; it is separate from the protocol key. |
| Protocol identity | A LayerX DID authorizes native activities and account operations. | The custody service holds Human and managed-agent keys and signs disclosed activities. |
| Owner EVM address | Binds the DID and submits Governance lifecycle transactions. | Signs the binding and lifecycle transactions on chain ID 125. |

The browser does not hold the Human protocol identity's private key. The one exception is the explicit `export-primary-key` security action, which is the only route by which a DID primary key leaves the service; see [the Human interface](/human-interface).

## Confirm account funding

Confirm the DID-to-EVM binding before funding. Retain the transaction hash, inspect the native balance and receipt, and check the recipient and amount. The native funding path resolves the recipient through the address precompile and checks the transaction receipt. A funding reference alone does not establish a successful transfer.

## Show evidence accurately

Human journeys report three rungs: `unverified` (submitted), `receipt-verified` (receipted), and `checkpoint-finalised` (committed). A receipt is final once its block is committed. Evidence returned by `GET /v1/evidence/{evidence_id}` includes its class, verification level, content type, and encoded bytes.

Continue with [owner registration](/identity), [the governed bridge](/bridge), [block commitment and proof verification](/settlement), and [Paxeer JSON-RPC](/json-rpc).

pages.title: Data Availability
pages.content:
# Data Availability

Read block availability through the agent runtime and verify supplied batch archives with the proof library.

## Availability makes replay possible

The proof library defines five batch availability classes. Given an authenticated availability root and provider chunks, a verifier authenticates the data before replay. This format describes supplied batch evidence; the agent runtime reads merged-node blocks through a separate availability operation.

| Class | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Activities (1) | Canonical accepted activities |
| Receipts (2) | Canonical activity receipts |
| Oracle (3) | Canonical signed oracle inputs |
| StateDiff (4) | Canonical state-diff material |
| Recovery (5) | Canonical recovery metadata |

Chunks carry at most 65,536 bytes. Each chunk states its batch number, flattened bundle index, class, byte offset inside the class section, exact bytes and claimed digest. A chunk is accepted only when its metadata digest recomputes correctly and its Merkle inclusion path verifies under the data-availability root. Verified chunks must appear in strict flattened-index order.

**Source:** `services/agent/crates/layerx-proof/src/availability.rs` — `AvailabilityClass`, `Chunk`, `VerifiedChunk`.

## Fetch and verify workflow

1. Obtain the committed data-availability root from evidence you already trust.
2. Fetch chunks for the batch from a provider.
3. For each chunk, recompute its digest and verify its inclusion path against the root. Refuse chunks from another batch, out-of-order chunks and digest mismatches.
4. Require complete bundle coverage and contiguous class offsets before complete-bundle verification.
5. Replay activities and oracle inputs; compare state roots and the recomputed account diff.
6. Attest only after replay reaches the exact committed result.

## Agent availability API

The agent runtime exposes an `availability_fetch` operation. Its selector is a decimal block height. The request also carries a requested rung, `maximum_bytes`, `maximum_chunks` and a `deadline` in Unix seconds. Empty selectors, zero bounds and expired deadlines are refused. The implementation bounds transaction bytes and transaction count for the selected block.

For an available block, the runtime returns a complete `transactions` class with transaction count and byte count, plus the height, transaction root and receipt root. A pruned block produces a partial report with a provider failure of `pruned`. Missing data does not represent an empty block.

**Source:** `services/agent/crates/layerx-agent-api/src/read.rs` — `AvailabilityRequest`, `AvailabilityReport`; `services/agent/crates/layerx-agentd/src/human_runtime.rs` — `availability_fetch`.

## Block availability reads

The merged-node reader checks the requested height against the node head and fetches that block. It returns the block's transaction root, receipt root and transaction count, or a pruned result when the block is absent. The runtime returns this block report separately from the proof library's five-class batch format.

**Source:** `services/agent/crates/layerx-agentd/src/read/availability.rs`.

## Refusals and recovery

Keep storage and proof failures as typed refusals. Chunk verification distinguishes batch mismatch, index mismatch, digest mismatch, inclusion failure, ordering failure and incomplete bundle coverage. Retry a retained selection or restore authenticated archive data; do not treat missing chunks as an empty batch or replace a verified root with an untrusted newer one.

## Ethereum and Solana mirrors

Mirror archives extend independent access to batch history. `layerx-mirror-publisher` publishes archives to Ethereum or Solana, while `layerx-mirror-verify` checks a receipt obtained from an untrusted mirror archive without a hosted gateway.

Verification validates the archive, binds its batch header to operator-configured trust, proves receipt inclusion and returns freshness. Archive provenance and freshness are separate from the receipt's signed outcome. Preserve the archive commitment, trusted header context, inclusion proof and checkpoint references for later audit.

See [Receipts & Proofs](/proofs) for portable offline verification and native state witnesses, or [Finality & Commitment](/finality) for how data availability supports settlement.

pages.title: Debug Transactions
pages.content:
# Debug Transactions

Diagnose reverted or missing Paxeer transactions with receipts, calldata, gas checks, traces, and reproducible local tests.

Begin with the transaction hash, chain ID, and the endpoint that accepted the submission. Separate transport failures, rejected submissions, and transactions that executed with a reverted receipt; they require different next steps.

## Collect the transaction and receipt

Set the shell placeholders `PAXEER_RPC_URL` and `TX_HASH`, then use Cast to inspect the recorded transaction. These commands only query the endpoint.

```
cast chain-id --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast tx "$TX_HASH" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" --json
cast receipt "$TX_HASH" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" --json
```

| Observation | Meaning | Next check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No transaction or receipt | The endpoint cannot find the hash | Confirm chain 125, the submission response, and whether the provider has indexed that height |
| Transaction present, receipt absent | Execution is not yet visible through this endpoint | Check a known-good endpoint and the sender nonce before resubmitting |
| Receipt status 0 | The transaction was included but execution reverted | Inspect the ABI, revert data, and execution trace |
| Receipt status 1 | Execution succeeded | Compare emitted events and resulting application state with the intended action |

A receipt is final when its block is committed on the BFT network. A timeout after submission does not prove the transaction failed. Search for the original hash first; a new transaction can repeat the application action.

## Check the sender and call

Read the sender’s native balance, nonce, and the current fee estimate. Set `SENDER_ADDRESS` to the sender recorded in the transaction and `CONTRACT_ADDRESS` to its target. The calldata example uses `store(uint256)` from `contracts/src/Box.sol`.

```
cast balance "$SENDER_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast nonce "$SENDER_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast gas-price --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast code "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
cast calldata 'store(uint256)' 42
```

Compare the encoded calldata to the transaction input. Confirm the contract address and ABI against the deployed version. PAX pays gas even when execution reverts. Increasing the gas limit will not repair a failed authorization check or invalid function argument.

## Simulate the exact inputs

For the Box example, reproduce a call with the original sender and arguments. `cast call` uses `eth_call`; it does not persist storage changes.

```
cast call "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" 'store(uint256)' 42   --from "$SENDER_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
```

A call at `latest` tests current state. It may differ from the state at the time of the failed transaction. A call at the previous block is also only an approximation when earlier transactions in the same block changed relevant state.

## Trace historical execution

If your provider enables the debug namespace and retains the required state, request a call trace. Inspect the failed frame, its input, revert data, and nested calls.

```
cast rpc debug_traceTransaction "$TX_HASH"   '{"tracer":"callTracer","timeout":"30s"}'   --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL"
```

Provider policies and node versions determine available tracers. The node accepts `callTracer`, `prestateTracer`, and `flatCallTracer`. For a `-32601` response, use an endpoint with the debug namespace enabled. For a historical-state error, use a node retaining the requested height. See [Paxeer debug methods](/json-rpc).

## Reproduce in a local test

Write a minimal test using the exact contract version, sender, and arguments. For ordinary Solidity state, a fork pinned to a known block can help. Set `BLOCK_NUMBER` to that height and `ANVIL_RPC_URL` to your local Anvil endpoint:

```
anvil --fork-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" --fork-block-number "$BLOCK_NUMBER"

# In another terminal, read the local fork.
cast call "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" 'retrieve()(uint256)'   --rpc-url "$ANVIL_RPC_URL"
```

Use Anvil for ordinary Solidity contract state. For Cosmos modules, Paxeer precompiles, parallel scheduling, or consensus behavior, reproduce the issue with the matching Paxeer binary in a [development cluster](/docker). The source RPC must retain the historical state needed by your fork.

## Keep a useful bug report

- Transaction hash, chain ID, block number, and receipt status.

- Contract address, exact source revision, ABI, compiler version, and optimizer settings.

- Original sender, function arguments, value, gas parameters, and expected state transition.

- Decoded error or failing trace frame and a minimal reproduction.

- Provider type and node version when available; remove authentication tokens from URLs and logs.

Reference: [Foundry Cast](https://getfoundry.sh/cast/overview/). Continue with [parallel execution design](/parallelization) when the issue is contention or throughput rather than a revert.

**Paxeer source:** `rpc/` — tracers.go (DebugAPI), tx.go (TransactionAPI), and simulate.go (SimulationAPI).

pages.title: Developer funding and allocations
pages.content:
# Developer funding and allocations

Request a bounded development allocation, track its signed treasury transfer, and verify the funded account before your first Paxeer payment.

## Choose the right funding path

The hosted allocation service distributes operator-approved development funds in its configured environment. A developer or agent authenticates, names a recipient identity and public key, and receives a funded result or a typed pending or refusal outcome. The service controls the allocation amount, treasury, eligibility, and quota policy.

| Funding need | Mechanism | What the result establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approved developer allocation | Authenticated claim backed by a signed native EVM transfer | The configured environment allocated funds to the named identity |
| Native account funding | Native transfer to the recipient EVM address | The transaction receipt and recipient balance |
| External-chain transfer | Governed bridge with configured chains, attestors and caps | The bridge transfer evidence for the selected chain and asset |
| Local account setup | Emulator prefunding | A local development balance for inspection scenarios |

A development allocation is scoped to its environment and policy. Funding uses the recipient's DID-to-EVM address binding and requires that binding to resolve before transfer. Use the configured hosted gateway for allocation requests; its availability is separate from the public node JSON-RPC.

## Developer journey

1. Obtain access to the configured allocation environment and an active hosted identity session.
2. Create or select a recipient signing identity. Record its public DID and 64-hex Ed25519 public key, and bind that key to the recipient EVM address through the address precompile.
3. For a direct HTTP claim, choose and persist an idempotency key. Gateway claims bind idempotency to the principal and starter-credit grant.
4. Submit the claim and retain the funding identifier and transaction identifier.
5. Resolve pending outcomes under the same request key.
6. Verify the transfer receipt and recipient balance before sending a payment.

## Authentication and roles

| Actor | Credential | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Developer or agent | Hosted identity session Bearer | Request an allocation subject to the session principal and quota policy |
| Gateway service | Dedicated service-claim Bearer | Submit a claim naming the authenticated principal |
| Allocation service | Identity introspection service credential | Validate the session and resolve its active principal |
| Funding controller | Control-admin credential | Authorize the funding operation against the configured treasury |
| Funding signers | EVM sender and treasury attestation authority | Sign the native EVM transaction and attest the durable funding intent |

The caller's session token is introspected as request data; it is never reused as an upstream service authorization credential. The direct claim resolves an active session subject. The service claim accepts its separate configured credential and supplies a principal explicitly. Keep service and treasury credentials on trusted servers.

## Submit a direct claim

```
POST /v1/faucet/claims
Authorization: Bearer <hosted-session-token>
Idempotency-Key: developer-allocation-order-01
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "did": "did:layerx:<lowercase-public-key-hex>",
  "public_key": "<64-hex-public-key>"
}
```

The JSON body accepts only `did` and `public_key`. The allocation amount is configured by the service rather than chosen in the claim. Use the key-derived DID that the treasury funding path validates. `Idempotency-Key` is 1–128 characters from letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, dot, and colon.

### Service and JSON-RPC access

A configured service caller uses `POST /v1/faucet/service-claims` with the same headers and a body containing exactly `principal`, `did`, and `public_key`. Direct and service requests for the same principal share its identity quota. The service route must be configured with its dedicated credential.

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "px_requestFunds",
  "params": ["did:layerx:<lowercase-public-key-hex>", "<64-hex-public-key>"]
}
```

The configured hosted gateway checks that the session authorizes the signer, obtains the principal's starter-credit grant, and submits a service claim. It requires the funded amount to match the grant before settling it. The `layerx faucet` CLI command, `faucet.request` tool and Rust `RpcClient::request_funds` call `px_requestFunds`. This is a hosted method rather than a public node method.

## Amounts and configurable ceilings

The native funding path places the integer amount directly in the EVM transaction value, in wei. The response encodes the amount as a decimal string; the default claim is not a whole-PAX amount.

| Configuration | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_CLAIM_AMOUNT` | 1,000,000 wei | Positive allocation size per accepted claim |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_IDENTITY_LIMIT` | 10,000,000 wei | Principal total per quota window |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_ADDRESS_LIMIT` | 10,000,000 wei | Recipient public-key total per quota window |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_NETWORK_LIMIT` | 50,000,000 wei | Network bucket total per quota window |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_WINDOW_SECONDS` | 86,400 seconds | Allocation quota window |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_NETWORK_REQUEST_LIMIT` | 60 requests | Network admission ceiling |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_NETWORK_REQUEST_WINDOW_SECONDS` | 60 seconds | Admission-count window |
| `LAYERX_FAUCET_IDEMPOTENCY_SECONDS` | 604,800 seconds | Request retention; must cover the quota window |

These are service configuration defaults, not a promised allowance for every deployment. The gateway additionally bounds its claim request rate at 30 per minute. The direct service derives network admission from the TCP peer; service claims use a principal-scoped network bucket. Forwarded identity or IP headers are refused rather than trusted as quota authority.

## Signed canonical funding

The allocation service reserves quota and an idempotency record atomically, then sends its controller a funding command containing `funding_id`, `did`, `public_key`, and `amount`. The core constructs an EIP-1559 native transfer from its configured EVM sender to the address bound to the recipient public key on chain ID 125.

Preparation reads the sender's pending nonce, gas price and priority-fee estimate, then estimates transfer gas. The signed funding record binds the raw transaction, hash, sender, recipient, amount and chain ID. The core persists a treasury-authorized intent before broadcasting, so recovery can reuse the signed transaction.

The core broadcasts with `eth_sendRawTransaction` and reads `eth_getTransactionReceipt`. It checks the confirmation against the saved transfer before returning a funded result. A failed receipt produces a refusal; an unavailable receipt remains pending. The source account must hold the transferred value and gas funds.

## Response verification and recovery

```
{
  "funded": true,
  "funding_id": "<funding-id>",
  "transaction_id": "<transaction-id>",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "network": "layerx-testnet"
}
```

This illustrates the default claim amount and the service's fixed `layerx-testnet` response label. Verify the transfer's chain ID separately; the label does not select a chain. Direct HTTP success is an unwrapped body rather than an `ok` envelope; its transaction identifier is optional at that layer. The gateway additionally requires a transaction identifier and a complete funded response before returning JSON-RPC success.

Retain the returned identifiers and verify the transaction receipt, recipient, value, status and chain ID. Confirm the recipient's native balance with `eth_getBalance` at the node; hosted `px_getAccount` and `px_getBalances` provide account views. A receipt is final once its block is committed. A funding identifier is a correlation reference.

```
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Retry-After: 10

{
  "state": "still_checking",
  "retry": "after",
  "retry_after_seconds": 10
}
```

Repeat the original claim with the same idempotency key and unchanged body after the carried delay. The service recovers the same funding identifier. A stored funded response is replayed; a different request digest under the same key returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. The gateway maps pending allocation to JSON-RPC `-32001` with `faucet_claim_pending`, never a funded result.

## Typed refusals

| HTTP | Code | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `idempotency_key_required`, `invalid_idempotency_key`, `invalid_argument` | Correct the request before retrying |
| 400 | `untrusted_identity_header` | Remove caller-supplied forwarded identity headers |
| 401 | `identity_required`, `service_token_required` | Authenticate with the correct credential for the route |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` | Recover the original request rather than modifying its body |
| 429 | `network_request_rate`, `identity_quota`, `address_quota`, `network_quota` | Respect the supplied retry delay and configured allowance |
| 503 | `identity_unavailable`, `persistence_unavailable` | Retain the request key while dependencies recover |
| 503 | `funding_rejected` | Inspect the destination and treasury funding refusal |

## Owner operations

Configure the allocation amount and caps, supply a funded EVM sender with gas balance, and provision separate identity, service-claim, and control credentials. Persist quota and idempotency state in the configured TLS Redis service. Keep the funding journal durable across controller restarts and retain its request digest bindings.

The service exposes `GET /livez` for process liveness and `GET /readyz` for Redis readiness. A ready response establishes Redis availability; independently monitor identity introspection, controller connectivity, treasury balances, and receipt recovery. Its hash-chained allocation audit records event, result, and funding reference without recording authentication values.

## Continue building

- [Send your first payment](/payments-quickstart)

- [Account funding and key custody](/custody)

- [Asset metadata and account balances](/assets)

- [Execution fees and fee limits](/fees)

- [Public payment API](/platform-api)

pages.title: Program Discovery
pages.content:
# Program Discovery

Discover registered programs and resolve current interfaces, lifecycle, accounts and signed deployment provenance.

## Resolve evidence before execution

Paxeer X discovery lets wallets, agents and applications find registered programs and inspect the version they are about to call. The hosted registry combines deployment records, a verified current protocol head and published interfaces. Each resolved program carries identity, version and freshness information that the client can bind to its preparation.

A program ID is a stable 32-byte identifier. The latest code hash, ABI, lifecycle and account bindings describe its current verified execution context. An application preserves both the stable identity and the version-specific evidence when presenting an action to its user.

## Start with the registry index

```
GET /v1/programs/registry
Authorization: Bearer <registry-request-token>

Response fields:
program_ids
state_root
observed_sequence
observed_at
valid_through
verification = "registry-receipt-and-current-head-verified"
```

Direct calls use the registry's mutual TLS connection and request credential. The index synchronizes protocol state and checks journal read authority before returning registered IDs. Its authenticated head and freshness window describe the observation used for that response.

### Resolve one program

```
GET /v1/programs/registry/<64-hex-program-id>
GET /v1/programs/registry/<64-hex-program-id>/interface
```

The first response includes versions, current lifecycle, upgrade policy, account bindings, source status and deployment receipts. The interface response binds canonical interface bytes and their digest to a specific program, version, code hash and ABI. Its verification marker is `deployment-interface-and-current-head-verified`.

## What a resolver checks

| Check | Required relationship |
| --- | --- |
| Program identity | The returned program ID equals the requested 32-byte identity. |
| Deployment | The selected version has a verified deployment receipt and matching code hash. |
| Interface | Interface version, code hash and ABI match the selected current deployment. |
| Lifecycle | The application handles active, deprecated and tombstoned status deliberately. |
| Freshness | The current time remains inside `valid_through` for the verified observation. |
| Value accounts | Account bindings and balance proofs match program state and the observed head. |
| Source | A verified source claim reproduces the deployed artifact under its named environment. |

Resolve related records against compatible current evidence. If an upgrade or lifecycle change occurs between reads, fetch the program and interface again before preparing a call. Keep the canonical interface digest and code hash attached to the user-facing disclosure or internal execution record.

## Node discovery with the CLI

The CLI reads the programs precompile through `eth_call` at `pending`. `layerx program discover` returns the program ID, upgrade policy, authority, code hash, ABI version, version and active status. Discovery refuses an inactive program.

| Node discovery field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `policy` | The program's upgrade policy value. |
| `authority` | The 32-byte program authority. |
| `code_hash` | The code hash returned for the selected program. |

The hosted registry returns `deployment_receipt_digest` with current-head metadata. The CLI's node read returns `source: eth_call` and `block_tag: pending`. Keep these evidence types distinct when presenting an action.

### Evidence requirements

A pending node view describes the state available for preparation. Establish a committed result from the execution receipt and independently verified block-commit evidence. Display the verification level established by the returned evidence.

## Application journey

1. Fetch the registry index and retain its observed head and validity bound.
2. Resolve the chosen program and inspect its current version, lifecycle and upgrade authority.
3. Fetch the matching interface and validate its program, ABI, code hash and interface digest.
4. When using the CLI, resolve the active program and matching interface through the selected node.
5. Resolve program accounts and source provenance relevant to the intended action.
6. Prepare the activity and disclose the target program, action, amounts, counterparties and fees.
7. Track execution and retain the resulting receipt alongside the discovery evidence.

For example, a treasury agent discovers a payment program, confirms its current ABI and active lifecycle, checks its permitted assets and accounts, then prepares a bounded payment under its capability and budget. A changed version or stale discovery window triggers a fresh resolution before signing.

## Lifecycle and account-aware discovery

Immutable programs advertise an immutable upgrade policy. Upgradeable programs identify their authority and preserve a numbered deployment history. Lifecycle history and exit routes let applications explain changes and route users through appropriate recovery or withdrawal journeys.

ABI 1 programs without value accounts declare `account-incapable-abi1`. Account-capable records supply proof-verified bindings and balances. Account profile 2 includes the owner established by its verified state. Resolve these bindings directly instead of inferring account ownership from names or UI labels.

## Source and publisher identity

Source verification links a mirrored archive, reproducible build environment and artifact digest to a verified deployment. Publication keys resolve through hosted identity, associating publication with a principal. Source status and publisher identity complement execution evidence: application trust policy decides whether a source verdict or publisher binding is required for a particular interaction.

Use the [registry source workflow](/registry) to publish archives and request verification. Preserve source digest, environment digest and deployment provenance when reviewing releases or generating a program catalog.

## Operate a discovery service

Back discovery with the canonical deployment journal, authenticated node-state connection and independent receipt authority. Keep the node receipt authority and its trust history current. Synchronization persists verified program state before advancing its cursor, and refuses regressions or incompatible state. Restart replay reconstructs the projection from committed evidence and refreshes its current head.

The default registry staleness bound is 300 seconds. Cache records with their `valid_through`, state root and version; revalidate before an economic action. A healthy HTTP listener does not itself establish fresh program evidence.

| Result | Resolver behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `404 not_found` | Treat the program as absent from this verified registry view. |
| `404 interface_absent` | Do not invent an interface; require published current-version metadata. |
| `503 stale_read`, `protocol_head_unavailable` | Refresh evidence before preparing a new action. |
| `interface_registry_mismatch`, `balance_registry_mismatch` | Reject inconsistent records and resolve matching evidence. |
| Inactive node discovery result | The CLI refuses discovery when `active` is false. |

Continue with [registry deployment and journals](/registry), [owner identity](/identity) or [agent spending controls](/agent-budgets).

**Technical references:** `services/platform/hosted/registry/src/routes.rs`, `services/platform/hosted/registry/src/head_attestation.rs`, `services/platform/hosted/registry/src/node_state.rs` and `tools/platform/cli/src/programs.rs`.

pages.title: Docker Development
pages.content:
# Docker Development

Local Docker clusters, state-sync RPC nodes, and monitoring for Paxeer X development and testing.

**Source:** `docker/`, `Makefile`, `chain.mk` (monorepo root)

## Containers for the complete Paxeer X stack

Chain development containers cover EVM and Cosmos execution. The monorepo also provides images for the kernel, hosted gateway and core, receipt authority, registry, agent boundary, Human services, bridge relayer, and application surfaces. See [archive access](/relay-archive) for retained evidence and mirrors.

| Image source | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `docker/localnode/` | Local chain node, genesis tooling and process supervision |
| `docker/platform-gateway/` and `docker/platform-core/` | Public receipt-verifying ingress and internal core boundary |
| `docker/platform-authority/` and `docker/platform-agent-boundary/` | Receipt authority and agent authorization boundary |
| `docker/platform-registry/` and `docker/human-service/` | Discovery registry and Human service components |
| `docker/bridge-relayer/` | Bridge delivery |

Hosted manifests under `services/platform/hosted/` define the service topology, persistent storage, probes, and infrastructure boundaries. The chain Docker Compose files below run their declared development topology; hosted services have their own configuration and dependencies.

Mount persistent state separately from runtime sockets and credentials. Pin image revisions and matching genesis artifacts. Publish the gateway through TLS ingress and keep core administration, signer channels, and node-local listeners private. Check `/readyz` and `/livez` where the selected service defines them, then verify an application receipt and its block-commit evidence. See [operator roles](/operators) and [settlement](/settlement).

## Prerequisites

### macOS

Install Docker Desktop from [docs.docker.com/desktop/install/mac-install/](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/install/mac-install/)

### Ubuntu

Install Docker Engine and Docker Compose:

- Docker: [docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/)

- Docker Compose: [docs.docker.com/compose/install/other/](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/other/)

## Four-Node Local Cluster

The base Compose file declares four validators on the `localnet` bridge. Each local node process requires `LOCALNODE_DISPOSABLE=1` and the same fresh `LOCALNODE_RUN_ID`, a 16–128 character identifier starting with a letter or digit and containing only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Supply these through the container environment in your local deployment configuration.

### Cluster Recipes

```
# Cluster recipe: rebuild the localnode image and initialize node state
make docker-cluster-start

# Rebuild the image but reuse an existing paxd binary
make docker-cluster-start-skipbuild
```

The recipes invoke `docker/docker-compose.yml`, which declares four `pax-node-*` containers and `x-websearch` (`pax-x-websearch`). Set `X_WEBSEARCH_HOME` to its configured data directory. Image selection uses `LOCALNODE_IMAGE_TAG` and `X_WEBSEARCH_IMAGE_TAG`. The node coordinator stores genesis, node homes and logs under `build/localnode-runs/<run-id>/`. These recipes stop the cluster and remove `build/generated/` before starting.

### Published Host Ports

| Node | P2P | RPC | gRPC / gRPC-web | EVM RPC | Additional TCP port |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| node0 | 26656 | 26657 | 9090-9091 | 8545-8546 | 26658 |
| node1 | 26659 | 26660 | 9092-9093 | 8547-8548 | 26661 |
| node2 | 26662 | 26663 | 9094-9095 | 8549-8550 | 26664 |
| node3 | 26665 | 26666 | 9096-9097 | 8551-8552 | 26667 |

### Monitor Logs

```
# Tail logs for node 0
tail -f "build/localnode-runs/$LOCALNODE_RUN_ID/logs/paxd-0.log"

# View all logs
ls -l "build/localnode-runs/$LOCALNODE_RUN_ID/logs/"
```

### Open a Container Shell

```
# List containers
docker ps -a

# Open a shell in a node
docker exec -it pax-node-0 /bin/bash
```

### Environment Variables

The Compose file passes the following settings to the nodes. The Make cluster recipes set `NUM_ACCOUNTS=10`; the initialization script defaults to 5 when it is unset.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `NUM_ACCOUNTS` | Number of development accounts to create |
| `SKIP_BUILD` | Skip binary rebuild |
| `INVARIANT_CHECK_INTERVAL` | State invariant check frequency |
| `UPGRADE_VERSION_LIST` | Upgrade version list passed through the node environment |
| `MOCK_BALANCES` | Use mock balance data |
| `GIGA_EXECUTOR` | Enable Giga executor backend |
| `GIGA_OCC` | Enable optimistic concurrency control |
| `RECEIPT_BACKEND` | Receipt storage backend |
| `AUTOBAHN` | Enable Autobahn optimizations |
| `GIGA_STORAGE` | Use test_only_dual_write with the EVM state-store split |
| `GIGA_MIGRATE_FROM_MEMIAVL` | Start in memiavl_only mode for a migration scenario |
| `GIGA_FLATKV_ONLY` | Start in flatkv_only mode; cannot combine with GIGA_MIGRATE_FROM_MEMIAVL |

## Single Node (Not Recommended)

The single-node recipe builds its image and launches one container. Its node process requires the same explicit disposable-run environment described above:

```
make run-local-node
```

Use multiple validators when examining consensus behavior.

## Compose Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `docker/docker-compose.yml` | Four-node cluster (base configuration) |
| `docker/docker-compose.monitoring.yml` | Prometheus + Grafana monitoring overlay |
| `docker/docker-compose.giga-mixed.yml` | Giga executor with OCC on node0 and standard execution on nodes1–3 |

## Monitoring with Prometheus & Grafana

The monitoring overlay requires `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE` to name a private password file. These recipes start and stop the cluster with the monitoring overlay:

```
# Start cluster + monitoring together
make docker-cluster-start-monitoring

# Stop cluster + monitoring together
make docker-cluster-stop-monitoring
```

The standalone monitoring scripts use separate configuration under `docker/monitornode/`. Their Prometheus listener uses port 9091; select them separately from the Compose overlay, whose Prometheus host port is 9099:

```
# Start Prometheus
./docker/monitornode/scripts/start-prometheus.sh

# Start Grafana
./docker/monitornode/scripts/start-grafana.sh

# Stop
./docker/monitornode/scripts/stop-prometheus.sh
./docker/monitornode/scripts/stop-grafana.sh
```

### Access UIs

- **Grafana:** `3000`, using the configured password

- **Prometheus:** `9099` for the Compose overlay; `9091` for the standalone script

## State Sync RPC Node

RPC initialization requires `STATE_SYNC_RPC_SERVERS`, `STATE_SYNC_TRUST_HEIGHT` and `STATE_SYNC_TRUST_HASH` in the RPC container environment, plus a matching genesis at `build/generated/genesis.json`. It validates the selected checkpoint against the configured providers:

```
# Build the RPC-node image
make build-rpc-node

# RPC-node recipe, after supplying its container configuration
make run-rpc-node
```

State sync restores a trusted snapshot and then replays subsequent blocks. Select a retained snapshot height and matching 32-byte hexadecimal trust hash; there is no fixed 500-block startup threshold.

**Scripts:** `docker/rpcnode/scripts/`

## Fast Iteration & Local Development

The node containers mount the source tree and Go caches. The declared image and cluster recipes support this workflow:

1. Edit code at the monorepo root (modules, consensus, SDK, storage, WASM)
2. Rebuild the node image: `make build-docker-node`
3. Restart the cluster: `make docker-cluster-start`

The root `go.mod` declares module dependencies and replacements. External Go modules, base images and system libraries must also be available to the build.

### Volumes

The compose files mount:

- `$PROJECT_HOME` → `/pax-protocol/pax-chain` (source tree)

- `$GO_PKG_PATH/mod` → `/root/go/pkg/mod` (Go module cache)

- `$GOCACHE` → `/root/.cache/go-build` (Go build cache)

## Deployment Scripts

Each node type has a multi-step initialization flow:

### Local Node

- `step0_build.sh` — Build `paxd` binary

- `step1_configure_init.sh` — Initialize node configuration

- `step2_genesis.sh` — Generate genesis file

- `step3_add_validator_to_genesis.sh` — Add validator to genesis

- `step4_config_override.sh` — Override config files (ports, peers)

- `step5_start_pax.sh` — Start `paxd`

- `deploy.sh` — Orchestrates all steps

### RPC Node

- `step0_build.sh` — Build `paxd`

- `step1_configure_init.sh` — Initialize for state-sync

- `step2_start_pax.sh` — Start with state-sync enabled

- `deploy.sh` — Orchestrates RPC node setup

**Scripts:** `docker/localnode/scripts/`, `docker/rpcnode/scripts/`

## Docker Image

The `build-docker-node` target builds `docker/localnode/Dockerfile` and tags the image for local use and the Compose reference. `chain.mk` selects `linux/arm64` when `uname -m` reports arm64, otherwise `linux/amd64`. `DOCKER_PLATFORM` overrides that selection.

## Network Configuration

The base Compose file declares a `localnet` bridge with fixed per-node addresses for peer configuration. Its published host port ranges map to the same internal node ports; application clients select the appropriate published RPC port.

pages.title: Local Protocol Emulator
pages.content:
# Local Protocol Emulator

Inspect local protocol state with explicit signing identities, account prefunding, time controls and snapshots.

## What the emulator provides

The emulator wraps the native core for local inspection and account setup. Its surface document declares the available routes and reports `payments.supported: false`. Local prefunding, time controls and snapshots support repeatable inspection scenarios. Payment and program execution use the merged node.

| Surface | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /healthz` | Check local readiness. |
| `GET /v1/sequencer` | Read the advertised native network ID and sequencer public key. |
| `POST /__emulator/accounts/prefund` | Establish local development funding through emulator account tooling. |
| `GET /v1/state`, `GET /v1/protocol/account-state/head` | Inspect local state; the account-state head route returns HTTP 503 with `principal_state_proof_unavailable`. |
| `GET /v1/dids/{did}/sequence` | Read an identity sequence. |
| `POST /__emulator/time/set`, `POST /__emulator/time/advance` | Set or advance local protocol time for deterministic scenarios. |
| `POST /__emulator/faults` | Inject a fault for failure-path testing. |
| `GET` / `PUT /__emulator/snapshot` | Export or import an emulator snapshot. |
| `GET /v1/surface` | Read the route list and declared execution capabilities. |
| Payment execution | Use merged-node `eth_sendRawTransaction` and `pax_sequencerReceipt`. |
| Local receipt reads | Existing receipt entries return HTTP 410; an unknown receipt returns HTTP 404. |

## Provision a sequencer identity

```
layerx --json emulator provision
```

Provisioning generates a sequencer seed from operating-system randomness and publishes its public trust anchor. It creates `emulator/sequencer.seed` and `emulator/sequencer.anchor` under the CLI profile directory using owner-only storage and atomic identity publication. Retain the paths returned by the command. The seed is secret; the anchor is the public verification identity.

Existing files cause `sequencer_seed_exists` or `sequencer_trust_anchor_exists`. Use `layerx emulator provision --force` only when deliberately replacing the local identity, then rebind clients to the new anchor.

## Start the gateway

```
layerx emulator up   --listen <loopback-socket>   --network-id 402   --sequencer-seed-file <provisioned-seed-path>
```

Run the gateway in a dedicated terminal. Set the listener to a loopback socket; its default port is 9402. Emulator control routes provide local development authority. Network ID 402 is the local default, separate from the merged network's EVM chain ID 125. Network ID zero is reserved.

| Option | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `--sequencer-seed-file` | Required provisioned signing seed. |
| `--listen` | Choose an IP socket address on loopback. |
| `--network-id` | Bind activities and client handshake to a local native network. |
| `--protocol-version` | Select protocol version 2 or 3; the default is 2. |
| `--time-ms` | Choose the local protocol time in milliseconds for deterministic scenarios. |
| `--prefund` | Repeat a DID, public key and amount tuple for initial local account funding. |

## Bind the CLI to that identity

```
layerx environment use emulator   --endpoint <emulator-url>   --network-id 402   --sequencer-trust-anchor-file <provisioned-anchor-path>
layerx --json environment current
```

Supply endpoint, network ID and one trust-anchor input together. The CLI waits for the listener and reads `/v1/sequencer`, then checks the network and public identity before accepting the profile. A profile can also use `--sequencer-trust-anchor <hex>` in place of the file. Subsequent selection uses `layerx environment use emulator`.

### Diagnose handshake failures

| Code | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| `environment_input_missing` | Provide the complete endpoint, network and anchor set. |
| `sequencer_identity_unavailable` | Start the listener and confirm the endpoint and identity route. |
| `network_id_mismatch` | Match client configuration to the running emulator network. |
| `sequencer_trust_anchor_mismatch` | Use the public anchor corresponding to the running sequencer seed. |
| `sequencer_trust_anchor_unreadable`, `sequencer_trust_anchor_malformed` | Correct the anchor path or public-key encoding. |

## Create development accounts

```
layerx key create payer
layerx key default payer
layerx account create --key payer --initial-amount 1000000
layerx key create payee
layerx account create --key payee --initial-amount 0
layerx account get --did <payer-did>
```

Key creation stores secret material in the selected credential store. Account creation in the emulator uses its prefunding route. Read public DIDs and account identifiers from the returned metadata instead of inventing bindings. This account setup is local to the emulator; it does not fund an EVM address on the merged network.

### Prefund at startup

```
layerx emulator up --sequencer-seed-file <seed-path>   --prefund '<did>,<64-hex-public-key>,1000000'
```

Prefunding binds the supplied DID and 32-byte public key to the local account setup. The amount accepts a decimal low component or an explicit high:low pair. Keep the signing key, public binding and DID consistent across setup and activity construction.

## Read merged-network receipts

```
layerx --json --rpc <node-url> receipt get <0x-prefixed-transaction-hash>
```

Point `--rpc` at the merged node's root JSON-RPC origin. `receipt get` calls `pax_sequencerReceipt` with the transaction hash. Preserve the response and independently verify its receipt authority and block-commit evidence. A receipt is final once its block is committed.

## Build programs and query the merged node

```
layerx new local-program
layerx program build --manifest-path local-program/Cargo.toml
layerx --rpc <node-url> program discover <program-id>
layerx --rpc <node-url> program interface get <program-id>
```

Scaffolding and building create local artifacts. Discovery and interface reads query the program precompile through the selected node. Program lifecycle transactions, simulation and calls use the merged network rather than the emulator's inspection routes. Preserve code hashes, ABI versions, interface digests and execution receipts.

## Move the application to a hosted profile

Keep emulator prefunding and local signing keys in the development environment. Configure the node origin for merged-network commands and a hosted profile for authenticated hosted APIs. A2A installation uses a hosted beta or production profile; MCP installation follows its enrolled daemon binding.

Continue with [the CLI reference](/cli), [platform API](/platform-api), [A2A agents](/a2a) and [Programs](/wasm-runtime).
